ideas.name: self-aligning hinged pad
ideas.description: A PLA pad hung on an M2 pin at the stock moving fingertip. It rotates freely within ±40 deg and has a TPU face, so it lies flat on the object's side at any jaw opening. The face is antipodal from 17 to 95 mm with no fixed pad angle, so no single opening (such as the banana's 70 mm) is the only parallel one. The pad body hangs 10 mm below the pivot, which offsets the revolute tip rise (+14 to +28 mm at 85–92 mm). A light torsion spring made from a TPU web keeps the pad vertical before contact, so it does not drop onto the object at the start pose.
ideas.test: A pads variant in design/fingers.py with a passive hinge joint (limited ±40 deg, weak spring) between the moving jaw tip and the pad, trialled on banana, potted_meat_can and the four boxes.

proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face / squeezed_down_out / fixed_jaw_missed: on the 81 mm-radius stock hinge the moving fingertip rises +12..+17 mm and its face tilts 44-53 deg at the 71-78 mm openings these boxes need, so it either lands on the top face (pushing 84-85 deg down on pudding, sugar, mustard), squeezes the 30 mm gelatin box down and out (31-52 deg down), or passes over the 34 mm tuna can with no contact.
proposals.principle: A fingertip on a swinging joint rises by R(1-cos q) and its face is parallel at one opening only; a finger can hold a side only if its tip reaches below the object's top. A slide keeps the face vertical and the tip at constant height at every opening, so contacts stay horizontal and antipodal.
proposals.hypothesis: long_slide at sector_radius_mm=50 opens to 103 mm (7 mm margin on the 96 mm mustard bottle) with the face at 0 deg and the tip at +1 mm at 35/55/85 mm, and squeezes 32 N vs 20 N now. Parallelogram rises +33 mm at 85 mm; prismatic reaches only 68 mm; 12 V servos are over budget and don't address the geometry.
risks: Round, rolling objects (apple, golf_ball, tennis_ball, racquetball, lemon, plum, strawberry, tomato_soup_can) are held between two flat parallel faces with nothing centring them. They should survive with contacts at the equator, horizontal and opposed, and 32 N of squeeze, but they might roll out along the face; proposal 2 hedges this with grooved pads.
dice / large_marker (17-19 mm): the slide's minimum opening is about 7 mm, so both are still in reach.
Extra wrist mass (~60 g) adds a little shoulder torque; the margin is still more than 0.3 N*m at 514 g.

proposals.edit: jaw -> long_slide (sector_radius_mm=48)
proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face (pudding, sugar, mustard), squeezed_down_out (gelatin) and fixed_jaw_missed (tuna). All of them come from the revolute jaw's geometry at wide openings. At 71-78 mm the moving fingertip sits 12-17 mm above the fixed one, which puts it at or above the box tops (+15 to +29 mm from the centre). The moving face is 44-53 deg off parallel, so it pushes 52-85 deg down. Tuna (85 mm) and mustard (96 mm) are also at or beyond where the stock jaw can still make a usable contact.
proposals.principle: A finger can only hold an object's side if its tip reaches below the object's top. Two contacts hold only when their normals are horizontal and opposed. A finger that slides straight along the closing axis neither turns nor rises as it opens. Its squeeze is servo torque over the sector radius.
proposals.hypothesis: Only one catalogue part reaches 90-96 mm with a parallel face and a fingertip that does not rise: long_slide (face 0 deg and tip +1 mm at 35, 55 and 85 mm). The revolute jaw can't do it at any servo angle. Pads can't either: even at 45 deg the face is +14 deg and the tip +14 mm at 85 mm. Parallelogram link 90 rises +33 mm at 85 mm. Prismatic tops out at 68 mm. Iteration 1 refused long_slide at r=50 only for a tiny wrist interference: 1.6 x 0.2 x 0.5 mm with the jaw at -0.17 rad. At r=48 the sector's pitch radius is 2 mm smaller, which is larger than the overlap, so it should clear. Interpolating 68 mm at r=30 and 103 mm at r=50 gives about 99.5 mm opening, 3.5 mm of margin on the 96 mm mustard bottle. Squeeze is 1.62/0.048 ≈ 34 N. Sugar box: 2*0.45*34 ≈ 30 N of friction against 5.0 N of weight. Shoulder load is 0.41 + 0.15*5.14 ≈ 1.18 N*m plus about 60 g of slide hardware, under the 1.62 N*m stall. Cost: $6.40 (2 lm3uu, 2 rods 3x150), 3 days, 216 machine min.
risks: Round objects (apple, golf_ball, tennis_ball, lemon, plum, strawberry, racquetball, tomato_soup_can lying): flat parallel faces don't centre them. They should survive because the tip stays at +1 mm, so contacts sit near the equator with horizontal normals and 34 N of squeeze against at most 3.4 N of weight. System 1 can re-centre the grasp height.
Small objects (dice 17 mm, large_marker 19 mm): the slide must close below 17 mm. At -0.17 rad the travel at r=48 gives about 8 mm of closing past zero, which should be enough.

proposals.mechanism: Two mechanisms. (1) The wide boxes fail with moving_jaw_on_top_face and squeezed_down_out, and the tuna can with fixed_jaw_missed. On the revolute jaw the moving fingertip rises +12 to +17 mm and its face tilts 44-53 deg at 72-85 mm, so it lands on the top face of boxes that are only 30-45 mm tall (pudding contact at +17 mm, top at +19, pushing 85 deg down). (2) The long_slide fixes that but lost apple, banana, potted_meat_can and tomato_soup_can, and the cause is the slide body itself. The carriage pressed on the side of the potted meat can at +41 mm (top at +42), and the rack pressed down on the top of the banana at +20 mm (top at +19). The carriage and rack sit too low over tall objects and hit them.
proposals.principle: A finger can only hold a side if its contact reaches below the object's top while everything above the contact stays clear. Pad reach moves the contact point 25 mm below the stock fingertip. With the fingertip-to-table clearance unchanged, the carriage and rack ride 25 mm higher: the potted-meat carriage goes from +41 to about +66 (top +42), the banana rack from +20 to about +45 (top +19), and on the lying soup can (top +34) the carriage clears too. On the slide the faces stay parallel at 0 deg and the tip rises only +1 mm at every opening, so the box contacts become antipodal.
proposals.hypothesis: The iteration-2 slide trials (r=45-48) gained gelatin, pudding, sugar and tuna every time and always lost the same four tall or elongated objects through carriage or rack contact. Changing the sector radius cannot fix that, so the change belongs in the pads. r=46 is the largest radius that has passed the wrist-interference law (48 and 50 were refused). By interpolation it opens about 96 mm and squeezes about 35 N. I set TPU to 0 so the pads take as little of the opening as possible, which keeps 90-92 mm pudding and sugar in reach. Friction is already ample: sugar needs 5 N, and 2*0.45*35 ≈ 31 N. A 2 mm V-groove keeps the balls, fruit and lying soup can centred. The pads cost $0, and the slide costs $6.40 with 3 days of lead time and about 232 machine minutes in total.

dice, large_marker: the contact is now 25 mm further from the wrist on a printed pad. These are light (5-16 g) and the slide's minimum opening of about 8 mm still closes on them.

proposals.mechanism: Two failure modes. moving_jaw_on_top_face, squeezed_down_out and fixed_jaw_missed all come from the revolute jaw's fingertip rising (+12 to +17 mm at 71–78 mm openings) above low box tops at +15 to +23 mm, with the face 44–53° off parallel. Separately, in the earlier slide-only trials the carriage and rack hit the tops of tall objects (carriage 36 N at +41 mm on potted, top +42; rack at +20 mm on banana, top +19).
proposals.principle: A finger that slides straight along the closing axis neither turns nor rises, so the contacts stay horizontal and opposed at every opening. Adding reach_mm to the fingertips raises everything above them by the same amount. A few millimetres of reach moves the carriage and rack off the tops of tall objects that they missed by only 1 mm.
proposals.hypothesis:
The slide alone at r=45–48 has already shown it gains all four low boxes. Its losses were one-millimetre interferences above the fingertips, and no sector radius can fix those, since all four r values lost the same four objects.

Pads did fix the clearance problem, but in iteration 3 they were set too long. At reach 25, and also at 14–22 on the revolute jaw, they hit potted's top at t=0.02 s and the tops of apple, foam and tennis. At reach 5 potted showed no start-pose collision. So an 8 mm reach gives about 7 mm of clearance for the carriage and rack and stays under the reach that caused trouble.

r=48 is the widest radius that wasn't refused for interference. It opens to about 99 mm before pad thickness, which covers sugar at 92 mm. It also gives the lowest squeeze among the trialled radii, about 34 N, compared with 36 N at r=45.

The pads add a 2 mm groove to centre the rolling objects and a 1 mm TPU skin as friction margin for the 370 g metal can at friction 0.35.
risks: potted_meat_can: the tallest held object. It is at risk both from a start-pose collision (reach 14 or more caused one) and from the squeeze force limit (the slide trials showed a 49 N fixed-jaw contact). Reach 8 is closer to the reach that was safe, and r=48 keeps squeeze near its minimum. The loop's refits can trim reach toward 5.
banana and apple: earlier rack and top contacts. Reach 8 should clear the 1 mm interference with margin.
tomato_soup_can and tennis_ball: rolling objects that were lost in earlier slide or long-reach trials. The groove and a 0° face should centre them.
foam_brick and cup: lost only when reach was 22 mm or more. Expected to hold at 8 mm.
dice and large_marker: the slide closes to about 7 mm, so these still fit, and pad thickness only shrinks the gap further.

proposals.edit: jaw -> long_slide (sector_radius_mm=50)
proposals.mechanism: Pudding box, sugar box and mustard bottle fail by moving_jaw_on_top_face: at 0.72-0.81 rad the hinged jaw's tip has risen 12-17 mm, and the jaw presses 20-36 N at 84-85 deg down on the top face (top at +19/+23/+29 mm). Gelatin box fails by squeezed_down_out, with the moving contact pushing 31-52 deg down. Tuna can fails by fixed_jaw_missed: at 0.69-0.76 rad the moving tip is already +11-14 mm high and nothing seats. The root cause is the hinge itself: per the brief, the face is 44-53 deg off parallel and the tip rises 14-23 mm at 75-85 mm.
proposals.principle: A face that turns with its joint is parallel at one opening only, and a fingertip on a swinging joint rises by about R(1-cos q). A finger that slides straight along the closing axis keeps its face parallel and its tip height fixed at every opening. That gives antipodal horizontal contacts below each object's top.
proposals.hypothesis: The brief gives long_slide at sector_radius_mm=50 these numbers: fingertips up to 103 mm apart; at 35, 55 and 85 mm the face is -0 deg, the tip +1 mm and the squeeze 32 N. That covers every failing width (73, 85, 90, 92, 96 mm) with a vertical face and no tip rise, so the moving jaw meets the side instead of the top. Friction check: 2*0.45*32 = 28.8 N against 5.0 N for the 514 g sugar box and 4.2 N for the 431 g mustard bottle, which is a wide margin. At r=30 the reach is only 68 mm, and any smaller radius would not open past the 96 mm mustard bottle, so the radius has to sit at the top of its range. Cheaper moves are exhausted. No revolute setting fixes this, because face angle and tip rise are intrinsic to the hinge. Every pad variant (13 trials) gained the boxes but lost the banana at t=0.02 s through the tilted pad's geometry, and the pad tilt is exactly what the slide makes unnecessary. 12 V servos are refused on budget and would not fix the geometry anyway. Arm load: 0.41 + 0.15*5.14 = 1.18 N*m, plus roughly 0.1 N*m for the slide's mass, stays under the 1.62 N*m stall. Cost: $6.40 (2 lm3uu at $1.2, 2 steel_rod_3x150 at $2), 3 days and 216 machine min, all within the $40 / 7 d / 600 min budget.
risks: Rolling objects (golf_ball, apple, lemon, plum, racquetball, tennis_ball, strawberry, tomato_soup_can): flat parallel faces don't trap a sphere by friction alone. They should survive because the contacts now stay at the equator, with the tip within +1 mm and the face vertical. The current hinge held them with faces 14-44 deg off parallel, which is a worse geometry, and the squeeze rises from 20 to 32 N.
dice and large_marker (17-19 mm): the slide spans about 7-103 mm over -0.17..1.75 rad, so 17 mm sits at about 0.03 rad, inside the range.
banana and potted_meat_can: both were lost only to tilted or extended pads pressing down. The slide has no tilt and no added reach, and the record notes that slide results cleared the banana before.
Extra wrist mass (about 60 g) on the 514 g sugar box and 370 g potted meat can: still under stall by about 0.35 N*m.
proposals.result: refused before trial: mechanism law (no interference): the wrist and the pinion share material, a region up to 1.6 x 0.2 x 0.5 mm (jaw at -0.17 rad, wrist rolled -2.74..-2.74 rad); parts may share material only at a bearing seat, within 10 mm of the hinge axis

With the slide, the boxes were gained, but the carriage and rack hit the tops of tall and low objects: the potted meat can at +41 mm with its top at +42, and the banana's top at +20 with its top at +19. proposals.principle: A finger can hold an object's side only if its tip reaches below the top while the rest of the hand stays clear. Extending both fingertips by reach_mm lowers the contact relative to the carriage, so the carriage sits higher above every object. A V-groove centres round objects that friction alone cannot trap. On a slide the face is vertical and the tip does not rise at every opening (brief: -0 deg, +1 mm at 35, 55 and 85 mm).
proposals.hypothesis: The long_slide fixed the boxes in every iteration-9 trial. It always lost the same four objects: potted meat, banana, apple and tomato soup. The cause was carriage or rack contact near the object's top, plus rolling, not the finger geometry. No sector radius fixes that, because the radius sets travel, not height. banana and potted_meat_can: if 15 mm of reach does not raise the carriage clear of their tops, they are lost as before. The loop's reach tuning should find the clearance.
dice / large_marker: the pad thickness reduces the minimum opening. At -0.17 rad the slide closes to about 8 mm, which is still below 17 mm.

proposals.principle: Two contacts hold only when their normals are horizontal and opposed. A face that turns with its joint is parallel at one opening only, but a finger sliding straight along the closing axis neither turns nor rises (long_slide: face -0 deg, tip +1 mm at 35/55/85 mm). The slide's hardware must sit above the tallest held object's top, so the fingertip contact has to reach well below the carriage and rack.
proposals.hypothesis: long_slide at r=47.5 mm passed the interference check (r>=48 is refused) and opens to about 15.5 + 1.75*47.5 ≈ 98.6 mm bare. It gained gelatin, pudding, sugar and tuna. Doubling reach to 30 mm lifts the rack and carriage another 15 mm above the contact, clearing the soup can by ~14 mm, and moves the potted meat contact well below the carriage. A 1.5 mm groove centres the rolling apple and soup can. A 0.3 mm TPU skin keeps the faces thin, so the 90 and 92 mm boxes stay inside the opening. Squeeze stays at about 1.62/0.0475 ≈ 34 N, so the 514 g sugar box needs about 5 N against 2*0.5*34 = 34 N of friction. Revolute pads are exhausted: 13+ tilted-pad trials gained the boxes and always lost the banana at t=0.02 s. Lower tilts leave the face about 36 deg off at 90 mm.

idea.name: self-aligning hinged pad
idea.description: A PLA pad hung on an M2 pin at the stock moving fingertip. It rotates freely within ±40 deg and has a TPU face, so it lies flat on the object's side at any jaw opening. I'm proposing three changes, all on the pads slot of the stock hinged jaw: two parameter changes to try now and one new part that is recorded but not tested.

**Why the pad angle.** Every angled-pad body on record (pad angle 38–45 deg) wins all four boxes: gelatin, pudding, sugar and tuna. Every one of them also loses the banana, on a force-limit contact at t=0.02 s, which means the gripper hits it in its starting pose. That loss stays the same whatever the reach (0–4.7 mm), width (8–10.6 mm), groove (0–2 mm) or TPU skin (0.1–0.8 mm). The only thing those bodies share is the pad angle. A 40 deg pad leaves the moving face exactly parallel at about 0.70 rad, which is the banana's 70 mm opening. There its bottom corner sits about 9 mm lower than the stock fingertip (stock is +11 mm). The stock jaw holds the banana with the face 40 deg off parallel and the tip higher. This is my best inference from the record; the logs don't show directly what touches the banana.

**The two parameter proposals.**
- **Pad angle 34 (on b06t2):** gives the banana about 6 deg of tilt and a higher moving tip. My estimates for the boxes:
  - sugar box at 92 mm: face about +24 deg (tan 0.45, under cardboard's 0.5)
  - tuna can at 85 mm: about +19 deg (tan 0.34, just under the metal's 0.35, so tuna is the risk)
  - gelatin box at 73 mm: about +9 deg, safe
- **Pad angle 36.5 (on b05t2):** a safer point for the boxes, with less help for the banana.

The follow-up fitting gets a clear direction from these two. Below about 30 deg the face reaches about +29 deg at 92 mm (tan 0.55, over cardboard's 0.5), so the sugar box would slip out.

**Cost.** Both parameter changes cost $0, 0 days and 16 machine minutes, using parts already on the bench.

**Other options I ruled out:**
- **Long linear slide jaw:** in iterations 9–11, its rack or carriage hit the top of tall objects (soup can, potted meat). Longer pads didn't lift the rack clear, and they lost the cup, foam brick and tennis ball.
- **Four-bar (parallelogram) jaw:** its fingertip rises +33 mm at an 85 mm opening, so it would press on the box tops.
- **12 V servos:** they cost $68, over the $40 left.
- **Mustard bottle (96 mm):** probably out of reach for any angled pad, since a 45 deg pad opens to only 95 mm.

**If neither angle keeps the banana,** the new part is the way out: a pad that pivots freely on an M2 pin at the fingertip and lies flat at any opening. It needs only bench items (M2 screws, about 3 g PLA and 2 g TPU), so it costs nothing to buy.

proposals.edit: pads (groove_mm=0, lip_mm=0, pad_angle_deg=19.5, pad_tpu_mm=0.8, reach_mm=30, width_mm=8)
proposals.mechanism: moving_jaw_on_top_face, the same failure on pudding, sugar, mustard and tuna. At 85 to 96 mm the hinged moving face leans 34 to 44 deg with its bottom swung out (brief). Its upper part lands on the box's top corner, pushing 69 to 87 deg down, which is outside the friction cone. Raising pad_angle fixes this, but every value that does so costs banana and/or potted meat. The cause is that the revolute face turns about 18 deg between the banana's 70 mm and the boxes' 90 mm. No single pad angle meets both needs: the banana needs a lean of about 12.6 deg or more at 70 mm (held at 29 deg, lost at 31.5), and the tuna needs about 21 deg or less at 85 mm (gained at 34 deg, not at 31.5). With the current 86 mm finger radius, pad angle would have to be ≤29 deg for the banana and ≥34 deg for the tuna, a gap of about 5 deg (0.08 rad).
proposals.principle: A face that turns with its joint turns by Δq ≈ Δw/(R cos q) for a change Δw in opening, where R is the fingertip radius from the hinge (81 mm + reach). A longer finger needs less rotation for the same change in width. It also needs a smaller q at any given width, so the fingertip rises less, R(cos q_ref − cos q). reach_mm is the only pad parameter that changes R, and the record has only tried 0 to 4.7 mm on the hinge.
proposals.hypothesis: I fitted w ≈ 4 + R_eff sin q to the brief's table (R_eff ≈ 99 mm now; about 124 mm with reach 30). The face turn from 70 to 85 mm drops from 0.23 rad to 0.15 rad, and from 57 to 90 mm from 0.49 rad to 0.32 rad. With reach 30 and pad_angle 19.5 deg (0.34 rad), the predicted leans are: 57 mm ≈ +6 deg, 70 mm ≈ +12.5 (banana edge), 75 mm ≈ +15 (apple, held at 11.7 on the 34-deg body), 85 mm ≈ +21 (tuna; the 34-deg body gained it at 21), 90 mm ≈ +24 (pudding; the 34-deg body gained it at 26), 92 mm ≈ +26 (sugar, borderline). The moving tip at 90 mm should rise about 21 mm instead of about 30. The bands now overlap, which no angle at reach 4.7 can achieve. Cheaper moves are used up: three pad_angle-only trials in iteration 13 gained nothing. Swaps are worse: the parallelogram's tip rises +48 mm at 85 mm, the prismatic slide maxes out at 59 mm, and the long_slide's rack hit the tops of six tall held objects even with 30 mm pads (record, iteration 11). Reprinting the pads takes a few grams of PLA/TPU, about 30 machine minutes, $0.
risks: potted_meat_can: its face at 57 mm drops from about +9 to about +6 deg bottom-out. The 27-deg body lost it at about +5 (squeezed_down_out), while the 40-deg bodies held it at −7.5, so this is uncertain.
